name: Executive order of May 15, 1884 restoring the 1880 Jicarilla Apache reserve to the public domain
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. Royce records that the President restored to the public domain the reserve set apart for the Jicarilla Apache by the executive order of September 21, 1880.
compensation: None for this reserve as such. The Jicarilla aboriginal land claim (Docket 22-A) ended in a stipulated final award of $9,150,000 on April 21, 1971.
today: The Indian Claims Commission held that the United States took Jicarilla Indian title without compensation on August 20, 1883, when the Army began removing them to Fort Stanton, and found the 1887 reservation, where they have lived since, virtually the same as the one created by the 1880 order. That taking is recorded under cession-1886-10-01-apache-eastern-bands and is not counted here.

openQuestions: This revoked an executive-order reserve. Under the 2026-11-08 rule that is not by itself a breach; the Commission dated the taking to the 1883 removal, not to this order.
The Commission findings and award were read through the existing record cession-1880-09-21-apache-jicarilla and were not re-read in full for this record.
The Jicarilla Apache Nation's own account of the 1884 revocation was not located.
